label: PF Backlog 600
title: EDP-19: Durable JobStore/OutboxStore + leases/heartbeat/retry/cancel/dead-letter; one-owner boundary vs WorkerGrid (L2, no second queue)

brief.problem: Jobs and cross-service events lack durable, recoverable storage with lease semantics
brief.what_adds: DB-backed JobStore and OutboxStore with leases/retry/dead-letter
brief.why: Reliability and exactly-once processing without adding a queue

objective: Provide durable, DB-backed JobStore and OutboxStore with leases, heartbeat, retry, cancel, and dead-letter handling, with a strict one-owner boundary against WorkerGrid (no second queue).
acceptance_criteria: OutboxStore provides transactional outbox consumed by WorkerGrid
Lease expiry reclaims jobs exactly-once (no double execution)
Boundary documented and enforced (no separate queue runtime)
SLO metrics exported per BI-PF-1314 observability
approach: Schema-first migration; DAO with explicit transactional claim (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED); heartbeat endpoint following existing pattern.
verification: PARTIAL: jobs table + JobStore (Submit/Claim/Heartbeat/Complete/Fail/Release) + /jobs API merged. REMAINING: OutboxStore (Event/outbox) + dead-letter.
risks: Accidental creation of a second queue violating L2 constraint
Dead-letter replay semantics undefined by consumers
rollback: Migration is additive; feature-flag consumers to fall back to pre-existing direct scheduling.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Create DB-backed JobStore/OutboxStore as new tables+DAO modules on the shared DB foundation (BI-PF-1309); lease/heartbeat modeled after existing /api/v1/engineering/assignments/{item_id}/heartbeat pattern; explicitly NO second queue system — WorkerGrid remains sole worker owner.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1314 (benchmarks/observability) at done for SLO measurement
conflict_findings: Boundary risk: WorkerGrid queue code must not be duplicated or second-guessed
DB schema contention with BI-PF-1309 migrations
duplication_findings: No existing durable job/outbox store in candidates (components=[])
Heartbeat API exists for assignments but is a different domain — reuse pattern, not code
Must not duplicate WorkerGrid's queue role (boundary constraint)
analysis.rationale: No reusable store exists; a new DB-backed component is genuinely required, kept minimal by the no-second-queue boundary.
assumptions: One DB, tables co-located with foundation schema
Retry is exponential backoff with jitter; dead-letter is terminal until manual replay
WorkerGrid consumes OutboxStore, does not own job state
risks: Accidental creation of a second queue violating L2 constraint
Dead-letter replay semantics undefined by consumers
missing_info: Which producers write to the outbox
Max lease duration and heartbeat cadence

context_review.reason: DB foundation and heartbeat precedent exist; only consumer specifics and policy values are open.
